### Key Contradictions to Video Claims
- **Safe fridge storage duration**: Cooked rice can be stored refrigerated for **up to 7 days** (USA Rice Federation: https://www.usarice.com/thinkrice/how-to/how-to-store-rice)[1], **4-6 days** (Riceland Foods: https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods)[2], or **3-4 days** (Consumer Reports/USDA guidelines: https://www.consumerreports.org/health/food-safety/is-leftover-rice-safe-to-eat-a8310482886/)[4]. No source supports a strict 24-hour limit.
- **Bacillus cereus risk**: This bacterium (not a mold, as video misstates) grows if cooked rice sits at room temperature >2 hours (danger zone: 40-140°F), producing heat-stable toxins. Refrigerate within 2 hours to prevent this (Consumer Reports: https://www.consumerreports.org/health/food-safety/is-leftover-rice-safe-to-eat-a8310482886/)[4]; Foodsafety.org: https://www.foodsafety.org/question/cooked-rice-shelf-rice/)[5]. Reheat to 165°F kills active bacteria, though toxins persist if already formed[1][4].
- **No "fastest growing mold" or visible mold mandate**: Bacillus cereus is bacteria/spores, often invisible; mold is separate and visible (e.g., green growth). Rice doesn't inherently mold fastest among foods[4].
- **No liver cancer/carcinogenic toxins from routine storage**: Video links Bacillus cereus and unnamed "carcinogenic" molds to cancer without evidence. Bacillus cereus causes vomiting/diarrhea (fried rice syndrome), not cancer. Aflatoxin (fungal toxin) is a pre-cooking harvest risk minimized by regulations, not relevant to cooked leftovers (FDA via Foodsafety.org: https://www.foodsafety.org/question/cooked-rice-shelf-rice/)[5].
- **No "Rice Act" in Japan 1921**: Extensive checks find zero evidence of this law banning leftovers or explaining "why most Asians never eat leftover rice." It's a fabricated claim; Asian cuisines routinely use refrigerated leftovers when handled safely.

### Best Practices (Direct from Sources)
- Cool quickly (shallow pan to 70°F in 2 hours), refrigerate in airtight container within 2 hours[1][2][4].
- Reheat to ≥165°F; freeze for longer storage (1-2 months)[1][2][4].
- Discard if smells off, looks moldy, or sat out >2 hours[4][5].
